paragraphs.title: God's Revelation and the Setting of Judgment

easy.explanation: Psalm 50:2 says, “Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined.”
easy.q: From where does God shine forth?

easy.explanation: God calls to the heavens and to the earth that He may judge His people.
easy.q: Whom does God call as witnesses to judgment?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “And the heavens shall declare his righteousness.”

medium.explanation: A fire devours before Him, and it is very tempestuous round about Him.

answers: To stand before Him in judgment
medium.explanation: God calls the heavens and earth so that He may judge His people, and He gathers His saints before Him.
medium.q: Why are God's saints gathered before Him?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the great storm surrounding God's appearance.
medium.q: What does “very tempestuous” mean in this passage?

answers: From God's revelation to the calling of witnesses and judgment
challenge.explanation: God appears, calls heaven and earth, and gathers His people for judgment.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in these verses?

answers: The judgment is hidden from His saints
The judgment is public and universal
The earth has no part in the judgment
challenge.explanation: Calling heaven and earth emphasizes the broad and public nature of the judgment.
challenge.q: What does God's calling of heaven and earth suggest?

answers: As the only witnesses of judgment
As those who made a covenant with God by sacrifice
challenge.explanation: God says, “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”

paragraphs.title: Sacrifice Is Not God's Need but an Expression of Gratitude and Commitment

answers: He does not need animals or sacrifices
easy.explanation: God says He will not take a bullock or goats from Israel's folds because all creatures already belong to Him.
easy.q: What does God clarify about sacrifices?

easy.explanation: The psalm commands, “Offer unto God thanksgiving.”
easy.q: What offering is the worshipper called to bring?

easy.explanation: God says, “Call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee.”
easy.q: What should a person do in the day of trouble?

answers: Because every beast and cattle already belong to Him
Because there are no animals in the world
Because only man belongs to Him
medium.explanation: God says, “For every beast of the forest is mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills.”
medium.q: Why does God not need the animals brought for sacrifice?

answers: Both express gratitude and commitment to God
Both remove the need to pray
medium.explanation: The verse joins offering thanksgiving with paying vows unto the most High.
medium.q: What connection does the psalm make between thanksgiving and vows?

medium.explanation: A vow is a promise or commitment that a person has made and should fulfill.

answers: Sacrifice expresses the worshipper's gratitude and commitment
Sacrifice replaces every need for prayer
challenge.explanation: God says He does not need the flesh of bulls or the blood of goats; He calls people to thanksgiving, faithfulness, and prayer.
challenge.q: What view of sacrifice is presented in this passage?

answers: Call upon God, be delivered, and glorify Him
Bring animals, remain silent, and forget Him
Hide the trouble, flee, and make a vow
challenge.explanation: God says, “Call upon me... I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.”
challenge.q: What sequence does God give for the day of trouble?

answers: The animals belong to God, while thanksgiving is the worshipper's response to Him
The animals do not belong to God, while thanksgiving belongs only to priests
Animals and thanksgiving are presented as exactly the same
challenge.explanation: God owns all creatures, while He calls the worshipper to respond with thanksgiving and faithful obedience.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between animals and thanksgiving?

paragraphs.title: Reproof of the Wicked and the Gap Between Words and Deeds

easy.q: What does the wicked person do concerning instruction?

answers: Those who pray and show mercy
easy.explanation: The wicked person consents with a thief and is a partaker with adulterers.
easy.q: With whom does the wicked person join?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Thou slanderest thine own mother's son.”
easy.q: Against whom does the wicked person speak?

answers: He speaks of God's statutes but rejects God's words
He knows nothing about God's laws
He obeys God's words but never speaks of them
medium.explanation: He declares God's statutes and takes God's covenant in his mouth, yet casts His words behind him.
medium.q: What is the central contradiction in the wicked person's behavior?

medium.explanation: He gives his mouth to evil and his tongue frames deceit.
medium.q: How is the wicked person's speech described?

answers: Speak falsely or maliciously against someone
medium.explanation: To slander is to speak against someone in a harmful or false way.
medium.q: What does “slanderest” mean in this passage?

answers: God will reprove him and set his deeds before his eyes
God does not know what he has done
The wicked person has permission to continue
challenge.explanation: God says, “I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.”
challenge.q: Why is God's silence not approval of the wicked person's actions?

answers: They begin with thanksgiving and end in prayer
They include evil actions, deceitful speech, and slander against relatives
challenge.explanation: The passage describes agreement with thieves, partnership with adulterers, evil and deceit, and slander against family.
challenge.q: How do the wicked person's offenses accumulate?

answers: Religious words alone make a person faithful
The wicked person does not know God's words
Using God's words is inconsistent with rejecting His instruction
challenge.explanation: The wicked person speaks religious words while hating instruction and casting God's words behind him.
challenge.q: What does the use of God's statutes and covenant in this passage teach?

paragraphs.title: Warning to Those Who Forget God and the Way to Salvation

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Consider this, ye that forget God.”
easy.q: To whom is the warning addressed?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me.”
God promises, “To him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.”
easy.q: What will God show to the person who orders his conversation aright?

medium.explanation: Those who forget God are warned not to mistake His patience or silence for the absence of judgment.
medium.q: What may happen after God's silence?

answers: No one can rescue a person from God's judgment
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that no one can rescue the guilty from God's hand.
medium.q: What does “there be none to deliver” mean?

answers: Both honor God and lead toward His salvation
Both prevent a person from calling upon God
medium.explanation: Offering praise glorifies God, and ordering one's conduct rightly leads to seeing His salvation.
medium.q: What is the relationship between praise and the right way of life?

answers: Those who forget God face warning, while those who offer praise glorify Him
Those who forget God offer praise, while others forget Him
challenge.explanation: The passage warns those who forget God and commends the person who offers praise and lives rightly.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the two kinds of people in these verses?

answers: Praise alone is sufficient without changed conduct
True gratitude is connected with walking in a right way
Right conduct removes the need for praise
challenge.explanation: The verse connects glorifying God through praise with ordering one's conversation aright.
challenge.q: What does the connection between praise and right conduct suggest?

answers: To urge them to understand judgment and honor God through praise and right conduct
To teach that people have no responsibility for their actions
To command people to stop giving thanks
challenge.explanation: The warning calls people to consider the seriousness of judgment and to turn toward praise and righteous conduct.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the warning to those who forget God?

short_answers.question: According to Psalm 50:14-15, what should a person offer to God and do in the day of trouble?
short_answers.answer: Offer thanksgiving, pay vows to the most High, and call upon God.
short_answers.explanation: The passage commands thanksgiving and faithful commitment, then promises deliverance to those who call upon God.

short_answers.question: What mistake did the wicked person make about God's silence?
short_answers.answer: He thought God was altogether like himself and therefore approved of his actions.
short_answers.explanation: The wicked person wrongly interpreted God's silence as agreement, but God promised to reprove him.

short_answers.question: What does God promise to the person who orders his conversation aright?
short_answers.answer: God will show him His salvation.
short_answers.explanation: Psalm 50:23 ends with the promise that God will show His salvation to the person who lives rightly.
